_note: How the fidelity gate ARRIVES at a screen. One entry per in-scope screen
id: which door, which route, and which login gets there. Extending the
gate to another journey is adding entries here — never editing the gate.
arrive: 'anon' (no login), 'worker' (#login-grace), 'field' ([data-login]),
'console:<persona-key>' (the console's persona card, by data-persona), or
'flow:<name>' — a scripted-flow arrival (#179): the gate drives the real
flow first (real POSTs, a unique organisation per arrival) and lands on
the route with the session state the screen holds per-session. Depths:
flow:onboarding (registered), flow:onboarding-terms (registered, with a
second published set so the terms catalogue has 'other sets'),
flow:onboarding-invited (registered + a project's real invitation),
flow:onboarding-terms-request (terms requested, on the checks step),
flow:onboarding-approved (submitted + the operator's real decision),
flow:onboarding-project (approved + invitation accepted, grant minted),
flow:onboarding-wider-request (approved + wider set published + request
opened), flow:onboarding-wider-submitted (documents declared + submitted),
flow:admissions-queue (registered, then signed in as the instance
administrator — the operator's side of the same registration),
flow:admissions-review (as admissions-queue, landing on the registered
organisation's own #/admissions/:pid detail; the route is per-run, so the
map's route stays '' and the flow lands the page itself).
The workers wave adds worker-door depths, every one over real writes:
flow:share-pending (a presentation request minted by the verifier org,
landing on the worker's decision surface with two lines left ticked),
flow:share-decided (the same, decided by the subject's own voice, landing
on the sent view), flow:recovery-confirmer / flow:recovery-progress /
flow:recovery-refused (a nominated contact, an OPEN recovery, and for the
refused depth a recorded refusal, viewed as the signed-in supervisor),
and flow:anchor-arrival (the story's unanchored worker's first dev
sign-in — the binding append itself — landing on #/added). The funders
wave (#193) adds flow:funders-rate (owner assigned, signed in as the
rate owner), flow:funders-rate-published (as funders-rate, then priced
and published — the target route decides whether it lands on the
publish or the standing screen), flow:funders-mechanism (a fresh project,
the payment mechanism owner signed in, a mechanism created on it,
landing on whichever mech/* screen the entry names), flow:funders-held
(as funders-mechanism, then a real batch confirmed while the mechanism
sits configured-not-live, landing on the invariant screen with a real
HELD instruction on it) and flow:funders-live (every activation
condition completed for real, then activated). These take their route
themselves rather than through the generic post-flow reload: the
console's persona token and selected project both live in in-memory
state, which a reload would erase, same as flow:admissions-*.
route: the hash route inside the door, or '' for the door's entry screen.
A screen with no entry here is out of the gate's scope and is reported as
such — the gate never silently passes a screen it did not visit.

scope.why: Phase 1 is scoped to J3 — setting up a project (P-1 Org Admin, P-2 Project Configurator) — plus the five connective-tissue screens our own design adds (docs/design/j3-connective-tissue/README.md). The G-2 wave adds the org onboarding journey (g2_1..g2_13; g2_2/g2_3 do not exist in the reference): the onboarding door is deliberately reachable with no persona (#20, #155 phase D) — g2_1 arrives anon, and every screen past it arrives by a flow: mode (#179), because the flow's state is session-scoped by design and only driving the real flow can honestly put a screen in the state its spec draws. The G-1 wave (#187) adds the instance walk (g1_1..g1_6, console:instance — the screens read instance state, so a cold load is honest) and the operator's admission review (g4_1..g4_3, flow:admissions-* — the queue needs a real pending registration, so the arrival registers one first). The rest of the g4 journey (g4_4..g4_7) stays out of the declared scope: g4_6 is a custodian-console screen an earlier wave built to its own rail, and holding it to the reference's G-4 rail is its own piece of work, not this close-out's. The workers wave (#189/#190) adds the nine screens it flipped — w1_19/w1_15/w1_20 (per-share consent), w1_7 (nomination), w4_1..w4_3 (the confirmer), w1_4 (the no-document route) and w1_17 (the anchor arrival) — as picked entries rather than whole w1/w4 journeys, because the rest of w1 was flipped by earlier waves before the gate reached the worker door and holding all of it to spec is its own piece of work. Every one is session-scoped, so all but w1_7 and w1_4 arrive by flow: modes that drive the real presentation-request, recovery and dev-login writes first. The funders wave (#193) adds its eleven screens — f1_2..f1_5 (console:orgadmin cold for f1_2's assignment form; flow:funders-rate / flow:funders-rate-published for f1_3..f1_5, which need a real assignment and a real published rate behind them) and f2_4..f2_10 (flow:funders-mechanism / flow:funders-held / flow:funders-live — a real mechanism, then the invariant held instruction, then a full activation, each on the flow's own fresh project). Screens the ledger does not call implemented skip with the ledger's own gap note.

g1_1.note: the stand-up front door reads GET /v1/instance — deployment state, no session, so a cold load is the honest arrival

g1_5.note: ledger says compressed (design finding #185: no instance-level invitation primitive), so the gate skips with that note

g4_1.note: #/admissions — the queue must have a real pending row, so the arrival registers an organisation first, signs in as the instance administrator, and lands the page itself (the console token is in-memory, so the gate's post-flow reload would sign the reviewer out)

g4_2.note: #/admissions/:pid — the pid is the arrival's own registration, so the flow lands the page itself

g4_3.note: same detail screen as g4_2: the approve step is the pending registration's decision card

g2_4.note: the decided registration, read back: state, exact terms version, decider

g2_5.note: the org's real (empty) invitation inbox, read back — 'stands alone' is true of a fresh registration

g2_6.note: held permissions vs other published sets, read live; the request door opens only after approval, so the arrival sits after the operator's decision

g2_7.note: declared {kind, ref, hash} references via PUT .../documents, never an upload; needs the open request the wider screen minted

g2_8.note: the submitted request read whole; Withdraw is POST .../withdraw

g2_9.note: inbox from GET .../invitations with a real offer waiting — the seeded project sends it through the real endpoint

g2_10.note: the accepted invitation and the grant the acceptance minted, read back

g2_11.note: the published-terms catalogue for the session's application; a second set is published so 'other sets you could ask for' has something true to say

g2_12.note: checks are recorded verdicts with named owners from GET .../terms-requests/{id}, no fake automation; honestly empty on a fresh application

g2_13.note: the approved terminal state of the same status screen as g2_4

w1_19.note: the reference's who-is-asking frame: its buttons and callouts live on the decision surface (#/shares/:id), which one console surface serves together with w1_15; the inbox arrival at #/shares (the ledger's route) is asserted by the apps.spec.js presentation walk. The request id is per-run, so the flow lands the page itself

w1_15.note: #/shares/:id — the per-line consent decision on a REQUESTED share the flow just minted through the real verification service

w1_20.note: #/shares/:id/sent — the decided share, read back from the same record the verifier's face reads

w4_1.note: #/vouch — the confirmer's inbox needs an OPEN recovery naming the signed-in nominee, so the flow nominates and opens one through the real registry doors, then signs in as the supervisor

w4_2.note: #/vouch/:id — the live quorum read; the recovery id is per-run, so the flow lands the page itself

w4_3.note: #/vouch/:id/refused — the refusal the flow records through POST .../refusals, held OPEN with its owner

w1_4.note: the no-document route: every asserted facet renders before the form is submitted, so the honest arrival is the route the register frame's own button opens

w1_17.note: #/added — the anchor-arrival moment belongs to the story's unanchored worker, whose first dev sign-in appends the binding; the flow signs in as her, not as Grace

f1_3.note: the unit of work is a real field of the seeded definition, but authoring needs the assignment written first; the flow assigns the org itself as owner through the console's own act, then signs in as the rate owner and lands the page itself (the console token is in-memory, so the gate's post-flow reload would sign the owner back out, same reason g4_1 lands itself)

f1_4.note: the published-versions list needs at least one publish behind it; the flow publishes through the screen's own act before landing itself

f1_5.note: the derived standing needs the same published rate

f2_4.note: the mechanism must exist (owner named) before a test disbursement has anywhere to land; the flow creates it through the screen's own act on a fresh project and lands the page itself (the console's selected project lives in in-memory state, not sessionStorage — a post-return reload would reset it to the fixture project and lose the flow's own, same reason the mechanism modes below take their route themselves)

f2_5.note: the recon export is real but keyed to a mechanism; needs the same configured (not live) mechanism as f2_4

f2_6.note: the advisory statement's limits render once a mechanism exists for the signed-in owner

f2_7.note: the batching choice screen reads/records against the mechanism created by the flow

f2_8.note: the four conditions are read against a real mechanism; unmet, the refusal renders readably

f2_9.note: the invariant screen needs a real HELD instruction carrying mechanism_not_live — the flow drives a batch through evidence and the worker's own confirm exit while the mechanism sits configured, not live, exactly as the funders walk proves W4

f2_10.note: the last gate: the flow completes every activation condition (test disbursement, recon agreement, statement agreement, batching choice, verification submitted+recorded) and activates, so the release-on-activation state is real
